3.0.s.en: 1. The removal of the stay of bread and the stay of water:

3.0.0.en: “For, behold, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water.” [1].

3.0.1.en: When God allows Jerusalem and the children of Judah, His people, the bride, to come into want of bread and water, He breaks the stay and the staff, that she may perhaps return and think of leaning upon her Beloved (Song 8:5), so as to find in Him her satisfaction and her quenching of thirst.

3.0.2.en: God took away from His people the smell of the meat, the leeks and the onions by bringing them out of Egypt, but He gave them the heavenly manna in the wilderness and led them to a land flowing with milk and honey; He deprived them of the waters of the canals in order to present to them the Rock that followed them, flowing with water, and that Rock was Christ (1 Cor 10:4). God deprives us of temporal support so that He Himself may become our support and our heavenly bread and the living fountain who waters our souls with all their powers.

3.0.3.en: Here the prophet threatens the occurrence of a famine as a fruit of disobedience (Lev 26; Deut 28), and this was fulfilled in history at the destruction of Samaria and Jerusalem.

3.0.4.en: What is more serious is the occurrence of a hunger for the word of God, as it came in the prophet Amos: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord GOD, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD” (Amos 8:11).

3.0.5.en: * (The word of God) is food for the soul, its ornament and its safety; so in not listening to it there is famine and deprivation!

3.1.0.en: 2 The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent, and the ancient, 3 The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator. 4 And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them. 5 And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable. 6 When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand: 7 In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people. 8 For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory. 9 The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves. 10 Say ye to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings. 11 Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill with him: for the reward of his hands shall be given him. 12 As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths. 13 The LORD standeth up to plead, and standeth to judge the people. 14 The LORD will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses. 15 What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord GOD of hosts.

3.1.1.en: God raised up for His people mature leaders able to work, such as Moses, great among the prophets, David the righteous king, Deborah the prophetess and judge, and so on. But the people went astray together with their military, judicial, civil and spiritual leaders. They relied on the human arm, with its abilities and thought, and supposed that they were succeeding and advancing in spite of the corruption that had befallen them and their leaders. For this reason God removed from them the mature and wise leaders, leaving them to set up for themselves weak and incapable leaders, that they might realize their need of divine help even for the enjoyment of living and strong leaders.

3.1.2.en: “(He takes away) the mighty man (the Almighty), and the man of war; the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent (the one who manages affairs), and the ancient, the captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator (skilled in speech)” [2-3].

3.1.3.en: Perhaps by their removal he did not mean their expulsion or their death, but the stripping of them of the abilities and capacities they had been given: the mighty are weakened, the men of war collapse before the enemy, the judges lose wisdom, the insight of the false prophets is corrupted, and so on. In this way the people reap the fruit of their reliance on the human arm, finding themselves collapsed within and without.

3.1.4.en: This is what befalls the person who rejects God's work in him: divine grace (the Almighty) is taken away from him; he is deprived of fellowship with the heavenly ones (the spiritual men of war), so that he finds himself without divine help or heavenly support; he loses the gifts of the Spirit, such as wisdom (the judge) and discernment (the prophet), and he cannot make a decision (the removal of the prudent and the ancient); he feels failure even in his temporal work (the removal of the skilled artificer); and he is unable even to speak (the removal of the eloquent orator). In other words, a person loses his life and even his natural abilities, to live in inner emptiness, corruption and failure, in spite of the outward appearances of strength, wisdom, wealth and success that he bears.

3.1.5.en: Now, when God removes the mature leaders and a person loses the grace of God, what happens?

3.2.0.en: A. “And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them” [4]. When Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned, he accepted the hasty, violent and extreme counsel of the young men and rejected the wise, balanced counsel of the elders, which was full of love and gentleness (1 Kgs 12); so the people were divided, civil wars came upon the tribes, and enmity prevailed instead of love and unity.

3.2.1.en: God loves the young; He supports them and seeks their continual growth. But what He meant here by children and babes is spiritual and intellectual immaturity. John the Baptist was a spiritually mature unborn child, who bore witness to the Lord Christ while still in the womb of the Virgin Mary, whereas many of the scribes, Pharisees, Sadducees and priests were mature in years but not in spirit, and so they behaved like children, seeking to kill the Lord Christ and be rid of Him. Thus we see in the history of the people of God, from its beginning until today, many young people who were mature leaders, while we find men and elders who behaved with the spirit of immature childhood. Therefore the Apostle exhorts all believers: “Quit you like men” (1 Cor 16:13), meaning maturity and spiritual strength, for it befits all believers, men, women, children, elders and youths, to be, in the Spirit, mature men.

3.2.2.en: Origen comments on the numbering of the people mentioned in Num 1, which included the men without the children or the women, saying: [The present text teaches me that if I pass beyond the simplicity of childhood, that is, if I cease to have the thoughts of a child, since “when I became a man, I put away childish things” (1 Cor 13:11), I say, I have become a young man able to overcome the wicked one (1 Jn 2:13), and I appear worthy to be among those of whom it is said that they walk in power... and I am counted fit for the divine numbering. But if any one of us has wavering, carnal thoughts... he is not worthy to be numbered before God in the pure and holy Book of Numbers.]

3.2.3.en: Perhaps the prophet Isaiah is referring to Manasseh, who took up the rule at the age of twelve when his father Hezekiah died.

3.3.0.en: B. “And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable” [5]. The sign of the loss of sound, mature leadership is the upsetting of the balances, so that the law of injustice prevails and the spirit of disorder comes upon the life of the community, as within the individual. For where there is no sincere and faithful leadership, each person seeks his own interests at the expense of others, and each one reckons himself wiser and better than the others.

3.3.1.en: I say that when a person loses the leadership of the Holy Spirit, the law of selfishness, injustice and rebellion comes upon him within, and he enters into countless conflicts between soul and body and between mind, emotion and senses; the body rebels against the soul to ride the whole of a person's life and lead it into fleshly lusts, with servility and humiliation before temporal pleasures.

3.4.0.en: C. Entering a state of extreme despair, in which no one will accept responsibility, so that each man takes hold of his brother and says to him: “Thou hast clothing,” a sign of accepting him as ruler, because handing over the garment to another is a symbol of a person handing over his body to the leadership of another. But because of the ruin that has come upon the country, with everyone unable to act, each one says: “Make me not a ruler of the people” [7], explaining it by saying: “I will not be an healer (a binder of wounds); for in my house is neither bread nor clothing” [7]. Thus all became hungry and naked, so who would accept the rulership? Who can bind the wounds of such a people while he himself finds no food or clothing? This is the natural fruit of one who seeks a human savior, supposing him able to rescue him and lead his life without resorting to the unique divine Savior. The psalmist says: “Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help” (Ps 146:3).

3.5.0.en: D. The loss of shame and of the fear of God, for they came to have an uncovered face that is not ashamed to commit evil: “They declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not” [9]. The gravity reached the point that Jerusalem sank into repeated stumblings, not out of weakness or ignorance but deliberately, to provoke the Lord [9]. Evils are committed in word and deed without shame or modesty. This is the picture of the world in the modern age, as many young people feel that the deviations they practice, in all their forms, are a natural right of man.

3.5.1.en: He says: “The shew of their countenance doth witness against them” [9], for merely looking at their faces reveals the marks of sin and their deprivation of the work of grace in them, and as the Scripture says: “In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil” (1 Jn 3:10).

3.6.0.en: Even if the wicked are visible and have become the majority, there is a holy few belonging to the Lord, whom God will not overlook; they are not lost and no harm befalls them. Therefore the prophet says: “Say ye to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings” [10]. In the midst of severe distress the Lord keeps His righteous ones, and turns everything that comes upon them into their good and their glory. Joseph the righteous suffered much, and his labors were the very way of his glory; and we see him say to his brothers: “But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good” (Gen 50:20).

3.6.1.en: God does not destroy the righteous with the wicked (Gen 18:25), but keeps His righteous ones in the time of trial; He hides them in His pavilion in the day of evil and covers them with the covert of His tabernacle (Ps 27:5); He knows them, for He has graven them upon the palms of His hands (Isa 49:16).

3.6.2.en: St. Justin comments on the prophet's words: “Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves. Say ye to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings” [9-10]: [Truly your hand is raised to commit evil, for you killed Christ and do not repent; rather, you still hate and kill, as far as you are able, those who believe in Him as God, the Father of all, and you curse us without cause, and you do so to those who stand on our side. But all of us pray for you and for all men, as our Christ, the Lord of all, taught us, when He commanded us to pray even for our enemies, and to love those who hate us and bless those who curse us.] And St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [They bound Jesus and brought Him to the hall of the high priest. Do you wish to know that this also was written and spoken of Him? Isaiah says: “Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves, saying: Let us bind the righteous, because he is troublesome to us.”]

3.7.0.en: They supposed that they were doing evil to the righteous, but they were doing it to themselves, and so they reap the fruit of their work, not as divine punishment for vengeance but as the natural fruit of their conduct and their life. “Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill with him: for the reward of his hands shall be given him” [11]. “Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap” (2 Cor 9:6).

3.8.0.en: E. The love of authority rather than the care of love: True leaders are like fathers who embrace all as their children and give their lives laid down for the people; but when the grace of God is removed, leaders, even religious ones, turn into domineering rulers who have no concern except to defend their positions and their authority with various justifications, under the cover of defending the truth, the dignity of leading positions and the ability to cut off evil. These turn from self-giving fathers into little children ruled by the “ego,” or into something like women (a symbol of bodily weakness) who seek control, for it says: “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths” [12].

3.8.1.en: Some scholars see that this was fulfilled literally, since some boys took the kingship in Judah and some women played grave roles in the management of affairs. As for the symbolic side, the guides here, especially the priests and prophets, were overcome by the spirit of recklessness and the love of domination, and so they turned away from true love and faithful care. In their hypocrisy these say to the wicked, Thou art righteous (Prov 24:24). And as the wise man says: “The place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there” (Eccl 3:16).

3.9.0.en: In the midst of this corruption, especially on the part of the leaders, God intervenes for the simple ones among His people, and stands up to judge them as the vinedressers who ate the vineyard instead of caring for it, rebuking them thus: “Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks? Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock” (Ezek 34:2-3). They seize the rights of the poor, as Jezebel seized the field of Naboth the Jezreelite (1 Kgs 21); they beat the people to pieces and grind the faces of the poor [15].

3.10.s.en: 3. The removal of the means of luxury together with haughtiness:

3.10.0.en: 16 Moreover the LORD saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet: 17 Therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will discover their secret parts. 18 In that day the Lord will take away the bravery of their tinkling ornaments about their feet, and their cauls, and their round tires like the moon, 19 The chains, and the bracelets, and the mufflers, 20 The bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, and the headbands, and the tablets, and the earrings, 21 The rings, and nose jewels, 22 The changeable suits of apparel, and the mantles, and the wimples, and the crisping pins, 23 The glasses, and the fine linen, and the hoods, and the vails. 24 And it shall come to pass, that instead of sweet smell there shall be stink; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of well set hair baldness; and instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; and burning instead of beauty. 25 Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war. 26 And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she being desolate shall sit upon the ground.

3.10.1.en: After speaking of the judgment of the corrupt leaders, he began to speak of the haughty daughters of Zion, who perhaps were behind the corruption of these leaders. The daughters of Zion had forgotten their belonging to Zion and to the Lord, and walked like pagan women in arrogance, with luxury and frivolity.

3.10.2.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [These words were not directed to them alone but to every woman who imitates them. Paul also stands as an accuser when he tells Timothy that the adornment of women should not be “with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array” (1 Tim 2:9). For the wearing of gold is harmful in every place, especially when (the woman) enters the Church and passes before the poor. Do you wish to be an object of accusation? Wear the appearance of cruelty and inhumanity.]

3.10.3.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that our life is a time for spiritual striving, not for luxury in dress and haughtiness in walking. It is fitting for us now to strive as in a spiritual battle, not caring for outward appearances but for obtaining victory and triumph, for the time of open glory will surely come.

3.10.4.en: Once again the same saint asks us to fix our eyes on our Christ, so that we care for the inner adornment that befits Him and do not seek outward things. [You have Christ as your Bridegroom, O virgin, so why do you seek to attract human lovers?!]

3.10.5.en: The prophet presents to us some features of the wantonness that marked the daughters of Zion:

3.10.6.en: A. Haughtiness: “Moreover the LORD saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks...” [16]. Pride took control of them, so they became haughty and walk with stretched forth necks, after they had forgotten their fathers and mothers whose necks were bowed under the yoke of bondage in Egypt.

3.10.7.en: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud” (Prov 16:18-19).

3.10.8.en: B. Wanton eyes [6]: They were occupied with hunting the hearts of men and capturing them, as a natural fruit of the emptiness of the inner heart, so with their eyes they set nets of death, for the wise man says: “And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her” (Eccl 7:26).

3.10.9.en: The word “wanton” in the original means that they beautify their eyes with a black powder, since the people of the East were fond of wide eyes surrounded by a black circle.

3.10.10.en: C. Wantonness in walking: “Walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet” [16], a sign of the corruption of the inner heart. They walk in conceit and pride and put “anklets” on their feet, or bells on their shoes, to draw attention to themselves.

3.10.11.en: What will the Lord do to these arrogant daughters who walk in frivolity and luxury?

3.11.0.en: A. “The Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will discover their secret parts” [17]. Baldness or a bald patch is, for a girl, a sign of extreme ugliness, for God gave woman her hair as a crown of glory for her, that she may live honored and beloved in the Lord, admired, loved and honored by her husband, so that she shares family life with him on an equal footing, being the body that the head cannot do without. But when she departs from the natural law with a spirit of pride and frivolity, she loses even her natural beauty and honor and becomes like one struck with baldness.

3.11.1.en: The uncovering of her secret parts is a figure for the exposure of the corruption of her nature, or a reference to her nakedness, with no one to spread his skirt over her, cover her life and give her his name that she may take shelter in it and be joined to him.

3.11.2.en: This is the state of the human soul fallen through pride, for it loses God's gifts to it, and the corruption of its nature is exposed, so that it becomes without beauty, strength or honor; the most trivial sins mock it, and mere imagination and daydreams make sport of it.

3.11.3.en: B. The removal of all the outward show of wealth and adornment: the tinkling ornaments about the feet, the cauls, the round tires like the moon, the earrings, the bracelets, the mufflers, the bonnets, the chains, the headbands, the tablets (veils, shawls), the earrings (amulets), the glasses (transparent garments for bodily allurement), the fine linen (costly undergarments), the hoods and the vails.

3.11.4.en: Thus He takes from her the outward adornment and the undergarments, that she may be in nakedness and ugliness... perhaps she will return to God and ask that He Himself cover her, and so the Lord Himself becomes her covering garment (Gal 3:27; Col 3:10).

3.11.5.en: God allows this discipline for the daughters of Zion that they may find in the Savior the secret of their adornment and glory.

3.11.6.en: Here he points to what befalls the daughters of Zion during the captivity, for he says:

3.12.0.en: “And it shall come to pass, that instead of sweet smell there shall be stink” [24]; after they were occupied with perfume and fragrant scents, spending much on them, they were taken captive by the enemy and carried to a foreign land, where they are absorbed in work without rest, so that the smell of sweat becomes offensive. This is what actually happened; as for the spiritual side, the proud soul loses its deceptive outward adornment, and the stench of its nature, its poverty and its nakedness are exposed, that it may perhaps feel the need of One who saves it and satisfies it. And as it was said to the angel (bishop) of the church of the Laodiceans: “Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see” (Rev 3:17-18).

3.12.1.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus speaks of the sanctification of the sense of smell in us, so that the fragrance of the Holy Spirit in us may not turn away from us and the stench of our own nature remain with us, saying: [Let us be healed also with respect to smell..., and instead of dust being poured upon us in place of fragrant scents, let us smell the fragrance of the anointing that was poured upon us, which we received spiritually, and which fashioned us (anew) and changed us, so that a sweet fragrance comes forth from us.]

3.12.2.en: The prophet says: “Instead of a girdle a rent” [24]; after the daughters of Zion had girded themselves with decorated golden girdles set with precious stones, they were bound with ropes to be drawn into captivity as humiliated women. A painful picture that reveals the fruit of sin!

3.12.3.en: “And instead of well set hair baldness”; as a sign of humiliation the hair of noblewomen is cut, to make them appear ugly.

3.12.4.en: “Instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; and burning instead of beauty” [24]... Thus sackcloth became their clothing instead of splendid garments, and a brand appeared on their foreheads or hands as a sign of slavery... for slaves of both sexes were stamped with a particular mark by burning, so that the master might know who belonged to him.

3.13.0.en: In brief, he expressed the complete shattering of their life because of their reliance on outward appearances and on the human arm. Therefore he says: “Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war. And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she being desolate shall sit upon the ground” [25-26]. The men died, the women were taken captive, and the great city became as though empty!
